ops.title: captain-hook collapses 7 peer roles onto daemonkit's 3 lanes, widening what several peers may do
ops.body:
Decided by yasyf, 2026-08-02, during P4.5 W1.

captain-hook models SEVEN peer roles over three requirements (internal/hookd/server.go:288-306,
hostTrustPolicy(); hostTeamID = "SXKCTF23Q2" at server.go:19). daemonkit v0.21 has three fixed
lanes — Control, Business, Serving — and no role concept at all. A handler cannot learn which
requirement admitted its caller: Request carries only {Op, Body, Caller, Session}, and Caller is
{PID, UID}. Verified against ci/exported.txt.

Three options were on the table. Rejected:
- Naming the matched requirement in daemonkit Request. Preserves per-role authority and would
  serve any consumer with more peer classes than lanes, but it is a daemonkit API addition and
  v0.21.0 is already tagged, so it lands no earlier than v0.21.1.
- captain-hook enforcing roles above daemonkit, with the role carried in the payload. No daemonkit
  change, but it separates the kernel-verified identity from the claimed role, so a peer that
  clears the lane can assert any role. A real weakening, worse than the chosen option.

CHOSEN: fold the seven roles onto the three lanes and accept the loss.

**What this costs, stated plainly.** Peers that were distinguishable are no longer. Any peer
admitted to the Business lane may invoke anything on that lane, where previously its role bounded
it. The same-EUID floor and the code-signing requirement still gate entry, so this does not admit
new processes — it widens what an already-admitted one may do. That is a security decision, not a
refactor, and it is being taken deliberately rather than discovered later.

Revisit trigger: if v0.21.1 ever names the admitting requirement in Request, captain-hook can
restore the finer authority without changing its trust posture. Worth doing if a second consumer
turns up with the same shape — the pattern (more peer classes than lanes) is not captain-hook
specific.

Not yet resolved for captain-hook, and blocking its migration independently of this decision:
the Swift half is pinned at 0.20.10 with role constants (HelperProtocol.swift:8-11) and changed
init signatures; there is no Go test job in CI; and its Go tests drive trust.RunVerifierChild,
which v0.21 does not export.
